title: 2004 AMC 10B Problem 10

concepts.label: Sum of first n odd numbers

statement: A grocer makes a display of cans in which the top row has one can and each lower row has two more cans than the row above it. If the display contains \(100\) cans, how many rows does it contain?

solutions.text:
The rows hold \(1, 3, 5, \ldots\) cans, and the sum of the first \(n\) odd numbers is \(n^2.\)

Setting \(n^2 = 100\) gives \(n = 10.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The sum of the first \(n\) odd numbers equals \(n^2\)
